question: Doubts on mandamus writ petition( no action in my police & private complaint ) - Please clarify my doubts on mandamus writ petition( no action on police/private complaint) 1) Can I mention police( govt officials) as the only respondents in mandamus writ petition or else can I write the actual main accused names also as respondents in writ petition? 2) Can I write everything that is described in my police complaint/private complaint as it is in my mandamus writ petition? 3) What is the fee of an advocate for mandamus writ petition? 4 ) Is there anyone who can help me in drafting a mandamus writ petition?( Rajahmundry, Andhra Pradesh )
answer: Dear Client,A writ of mandamus is typically issued by the High Court under Article 226 of the Constitution of India when a public authority has failed or refused to perform a mandatory duty despite being requested to do so. A writ of mandamus compels a public authority to perform its legal duty, and the police are considered a public authority. You can mention police officials or government officials as the sole respondents in a mandamus writ petition if they are responsible for the alleged failure to perform a public duty. The writ of mandamus is primarily used against public authorities to compel them to perform their statutory duties. The names of the main accused can be included as respondents in a writ of mandamus petition, but only if they are also a public authority or have a public duty that is being violated. When a writ petition is heard on the merits, the court considers the substance of the claim, the evidence presented, and the legal arguments to decide whether the petitioner is entitled to the relief sought. The contents of the writ petition shall include: a clear statement of the facts, supporting documents, the specific relief sought, and a duly sworn affidavit verifying the facts. So, you can mention the inaction of the police on your complaint or private complaint in the writ petition. The advocate's fee for filing a writ of mandamus in the High Court can vary based on several factors, including the advocate's experience, the complexity of the case, costs associated with court fees and other expenses, and the specific High Court involved. Hence, it is recommended to consult with an experienced Advocate for tailored advice and a well-drafted writ of mandamus to access justice in the matter.

Yesterday I had 1 beer (650ml) and was driving back to my house in Bangalore. I was caught by the RTO and was asked to take a breath analyser test. The first reading was 0.2 and the second reading was 0.4. At this time, the RTO issued me a challan for 10000. After asking for DUI reading slip, the officer refused. As per Bangalore City traffic police, they will not be prosecuting DUI cases where the reading is 0.4 or below. I went to the police station again today morning to get the DUI reading slips and the police refused again. Now my questions are as follows: 
1. Can I contest this challan? 
2. If yes, what is the process for contesting ? Is it complex and will it require representation by a lawyer? 
3. If I can contest this, what are my chances of winning?
4. If I can contest this and will require legal representation, how much will the legal cost come to? An approximate idea would be good. 
5. If I contest this, how much time will it take for my vehicle to be released back to me
6. Can I sue Bangalore police for wrongful seizing, harassment and torture?( Bangalore, Karnataka )
answer: Dear Client,Section 185 of The Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 makes driving under the influence of drugs or alcohol a criminal and non-bailable offence in India. The Government has made stricter rules under Section 185 of the Motor Vehicle Act. Punishments under Section 185 of the MV Act include a fine of up to â¹10,000 or imprisonment of up to 6 months or both, including suspension of the driving license. If the offence is repeated within a year, the fine can go up to Rs. 15,000 along with imprisonment of up to two years. The permissible alcohol limit while driving in Bangalore is 30 mg or 0.03% of alcohol per 100 ml of blood. If a driver is caught driving with alcohol in their blood exceeding the legal limit (30 mg/100ml), they can be punished with imprisonment (up to 6 months for the first offense, up to 2 years for subsequent offenses) or a fine (up to Rs. 10,000 for the first offense, up to Rs. 15,000 for subsequent offenses), or both. A preliminary or passive test is carried out by holding the instrument (breath analyzer) close to the mouth and asking the name of the person or to blow, which indicates consumption of alcohol (passive test). If the result is negative, no further check is required. If the result is positive, a breath sample is taken using the disposable straw and the printout out taken using a connected printer. Subsequently, the Patent ductus arteriosus (PDA) generated police notice is given to the motorists. No one can be prosecuted without a computerized printout indicating reading and a PDA printout mentioning the reading. No police officer is allowed to collect spot fines for this offence. The offender will be given a notice and directed to appear before the jurisdictional court, and he has to pay a fine there. In the stated scenario, you can file a complaint with the Chairperson, State Human Rights Commission, or the State Police Complaint Authority, which are independent bodies empowered to investigate complaints against police officials. You can also challenge the action of the traffic police in the court of a Magistrate. question: When court permits to beat a criminal in interogation?( Howrah, West Bengal )
answer: Dear Client,Although your query is insufficient to respond, however, it seems your query refers to the third degree method in police custody to extract information from the suspects. The term "third degree" refers to the use of brutal and inhumane methods by police or authorities to extract information or confessions from suspects in custody. This can include physical violence, deprivation of basic needs (food, water, sleep), and prolonged, relentless interrogation. In India, courts do not order or condone the use of "third degree" methods during the interrogation of an accused, as such practices are illegal and violate fundamental rights of an individual, and confessions obtained through such methods are inadmissible in court. In the cases of Shri D.K. Basu vs State Of West Bengal, and Ashok K. Johri vs State Of U.P., the Hon'ble Supreme Court had held that the use of third degree methods is illegal and a violation of human rights. If an individual believes he has been subjected to third-degree methods, he can seek legal remedies, including filing a complaint with the police or a Court of Magistrate.

question: In what case scenario court gives brainmapping test without taking any concent of victim or accused?( Howrah, West Bengal )
answer: Dear Client,A court, including a district court, cannot compel an accused person to undergo a brain-mapping test, as this violates the fundamental right against self-incrimination under Article 20(3) of the Indian Constitution. However, the test can be administered if the accused voluntarily consents to the same. In the landmark case of Selvi v. State of Karnataka (2010), the Supreme Court ruled that no lie detector tests, including polygraph, narco-analysis, and brain-mapping tests, should be administered without the consent of the accused. Article 20(3) of the Constitution states that no person accused of an offence shall be compelled to be a witness against himself and any such test can only be conducted with the express and voluntary consent of the accused to be recorded before a Judicial Magistrate. The Apex Court also ruled that the results of these tests cannot be admitted as direct evidence in court without the consent of the person undergoing the test. So, even if the victim appeals for it, in the absence of voluntary consent of the accused, the Court cannot pass an order for a brain-mapping test of the accused.

question: Can any court including district court allow lie ditector test for investigation? And in which circumstances it can be given if victim ask for it?( Howrah, West Bengal )
answer: Dear Client,A court, including a district court, cannot compel an accused person to undergo a lie detector test, as this violates the fundamental right against self-incrimination under Article 20(3) of the Indian Constitution. However, the test can be administered if the accused voluntarily consents to the same. In the landmark case of Selvi v. State of Karnataka (2010), the Supreme Court ruled that no lie detector tests, including polygraph, narco-analysis, and brain-mapping tests, should be administered without the consent of the accused. Article 20(3) of the Constitution states that no person accused of an offence shall be compelled to be a witness against himself and any such test can only be conducted with the express and voluntary consent of the accused to be recorded before a Judicial Magistrate. The Apex Court also ruled that the results of these tests cannot be admitted as direct evidence in court without the consent of the person undergoing the test. So, even if the victim appeals for it, in the absence of voluntary consent of the accused, the Court cannot pass an order for a lie detector test of the accused.

I have gone through the decision of Honâble Supreme court in the case of Vijay Madanlal Choudhary V/S Union of India in Special Leave Petition (Criminal) No 4634 of 2014 and also other judgements on PMLA. After reading the abovesaid decision and few articles by renowned lawyers on the said decision, my observations (some are copies from articles) are as under:
â¢	â¢ The Supreme Court upheld the validity of the powers under Sections 5, 8(4), 15, 17, 19, affirming that these provisions have a reasonable link to combating money laundering.
â¢	FIR is not required for investigation, though it is not mentioned in the judgement. This is affirmed by Honâble Delhi High Court in the case of Vir Bhadra Singh V/S Enforcement Directorate 2017 (3) RCR(Criminal) 576
â¢	The Courtâs endorsement of the reverse burden of proof places more responsibility on the accused in money laundering cases, which may make it harder for accused individuals to defend themselves unless they provide credible evidence of their innocence.
â¢	In  P. Chidambaram Vs. Directorate of Enforcement, (2019) 9 SCC 24, the Supreme Court has held that a âscheduled offenceâ is a sine qua non for the offence of money laundering which would generate the money that is being laundered. However, this judgment, nowhere states that the registration of FIR is a sine qua non. 
In view of my above observations, FIR is not a pre-condition for lodging a complaint with office of the Directorate of Enforcement. Alternatively Section 17 empowers Directorate of Enforcement is empowered to order for search and seizure of property. It means I can lodge a money laundering complaint directly with Directorate of Enforcement without lodging FIR with Police,
I sincerely request your team to provide me your opinion on my observations made as above.( Raigad, Maharashtra )
answer: Dear Client,Your observations are largely accurate and demonstrate a strong understanding of the legal principles laid down by the Supreme Court in  Vijay Madanlal Choudhary v. Union of India  (SLP (Criminal) No. 4634 of 2014) and other related judgments on the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002 (PMLA).Your observation is very much  correct. The Supreme Court upheld the constitutional validity of these provisions and affirmed that the powers conferred under them have a  reasonable nexus  with the object of preventing money laundering. The registration of an FIR is not a prerequisite for initiating proceedings under PMLA. The judgment in  Vijay Madanlal Choudhary does not mandate the registration of an FIR as a essential condition  for lodging a complaint or initiating action under PMLA.Moreover, The Delhi High Courtâs decision in  Vir Bhadra Singh v. Enforcement Directorate, and in P. Chidambaram v. Directorate of Enforcement,  the Supreme Court clarified that a  scheduled offence  is a sine qua non for money laundering, but registration of an FIR is not a prerequisite.To conclude the explanation I would say that your observations and legal analysis are precise and well-founded since the existence of a scheduled offence is the primary requirement and not an FIR, you may proceed with lodging a complaint with the Directorate of Enforcement (ED) if you have credible evidence or material suggesting the involvement of proceeds of crime. The ED is empowered to act under Sections 17 and 19 without the need for an FIR, provided there is reason to believe  that money laundering has occurred.

P.C. sanction is required for an offence committed by a public servant while acting or purporting to act in the discharge of his official duty, and not otherwise. After the amendment of the Prevention of Corruption Act, in 2018, it significantly extended the provisions of PCA and gave it the required edge to tackle bribery/corruption involving commercial entities/private companies. This provision covers all types of entities (including domestic companies, foreign companies, and partnerships) doing business in India. Thus, while the PCA, 1988 applied to public sector employees, the Act has been amended to encompass situations where private organizations and individuals can also be held accountable for indulging in corrupt practices. Further, the CBI investigates cases of corruption in compliance with the provisions of the Prevention of Corruption Act 1988, under the supervision of the Central Vigilance Commission (CVC). This can include cases of bribery, extortion, and other forms of corruption. The CBI has a special division called the Anti-Corruption Branch (ACB). This branch handles the investigation of corruption-related cases. The CBI can initiate suo moto investigations on the basis of information received from the public, the media, or other sources. CBI lays great emphasis on catching corrupt public servants who demand and take bribes. The process of catching such corrupt public servants red-handed while they demand and take bribes is popularly called the 'trap'. It is not a legal term. A set procedure has been devised in CBI to lay a trap against a corrupt public servant. The evidence collected during the process of trap is placed before the court along with the charge sheet and is quite important in securing the conviction of the public servant charged with corruption. question: Can sec 67A IT Act be compounded If the judge allows?( Mumbai, Maharashtra )

However, the High Court can make the offence compoundable by exercising its inherent powers under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 based on the facts and circumstances of the case. This issue has been decided by the Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court in the case titled Gian Singh Vs. State of Punjab and Another (2012) 2 SCC (L&S) 998 wherein it was held that the power of the High Court in quashing a criminal proceeding or FIR or complaint in exercise of its inherent jurisdiction is distinct and different from the power given to a criminal court for compounding the offences Under Section 320 of the Code. Inherent power is of wide plenitude with no statutory limitation, but it has to be exercised in accord with the guideline engrafted in such power to secure the ends of justice and/or to prevent abuse of the process of any Court.

question: Whether the provisions of Indian penal code 1860 and of Bhartiya nyaay sanhita 2023 can be levelled against the person in a series of offence( Aurangabad, Maharashtra )
answer: Dear Client,The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) came into force on 1st July 2024, replacing the Indian Penal Code,1860. Questions have arisen regarding whether these new laws apply to offences committed before their effective date of July 1, 2024, and how they impact ongoing proceedings. The Hon'ble Division Bench of Allahabad High Court in the matter of Deepu and Anr. v. State Of U.P . held that while new offences after 01/07/2024 will be governed under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), all offences prior to that date will be governed under the old IPC. The court observed that if an FIR is registered on or after 1st July, 2024, for an offense committed prior to that date, it should be registered under the provisions of the IPC, but the investigation will proceed as per the BNS. For investigations pending on 1st July, 2024, the court held that these should continue as per the IPC/CrPC until cognizance is taken on the police report. The court clarified that cognizance of pending investigations on or after 1st July, 2024, should be taken as per the BNS/BNSS. All subsequent proceedings, including enquiry, trial, or appeal, must be conducted according to the procedure under the BNS/BNSS. The court emphasized that despite the repeal of IPC and Cr.PC, liabilities and punishments under the IPC/Cr. PC will continue, but procedural aspects will be governed by the BNS/BNSS. The Hon'ble Rajasthan High Court in the case of Krishna Joshi v. State of Rajasthan & Ors. (2024) held that the law applicable on the date of FIR registration will govern the trial, even if it commences after July 1, 2024. The Hon'ble Kerala High Court in the case of Abdul Khader v. State of Kerala (2024) held that appeals filed on or after July 1, 2024, will be governed by BNS/BNSS, regardless of whether the trial was conducted under IPC/CrPC. So, given the averments of different High Courts, if you want to file an FIR against a crime in January 2025, that will be registered and tried following the provision of BNS/BNSS that replaced the IPC/Cr. PC.

The limitation for filing a suit for specific performance, as per Article 54 of the Schedule to the Limitation Act, 1963 is 3 years from the date fixed for performance. So, when as per the Sale Agreement the Sale deed was executed 25 years ago, the right of both parties to the agreement to file suit for specific performance against each other is now barred by limitation. The limitation provided under Article 24 of the Schedule to the Limitation Act, 1963, for filing a suit for recovery of money is also three years which now makes the claim of the buyer barred by limitation. But, as per Section 22 of the Limitation Act, where there is a continuing breach of contract or a continuous tort, a fresh period of limitation begins to run at every moment during which the breach continues. Accordingly, both the buyer and the seller can file a suit for money recovery and specific performance on the grounds of continuing breach of contract. The Contract Act does not make stamping of agreements compulsory, nor does it deem an unstamped agreement/contract invalid and unenforceable. An unregistered deed signed by parties voluntarily and counter-signed by witnesses even in plain paper can still be used as evidence for collateral purposes as per the proviso mentioned under Section 49 of the Registration Act of 1908. So, stamping is not mandatory for all sorts of agreements except when it has relation to an interest in any immovable property or monetary transactions involved. Stamping and registration of such documents are to secure such rights of the parties in a contract or agreement, and the Court also admits such documents as worthy evidence while adjudicating any dispute that arises thereof between the parties to an agreement or contract. However, possession of the property is also considered a determinative factor in claiming ownership of any property. Article 65 of the Limitation Act, 1963 provides a time limit of 12 years for a suit for possession of immovable property or any other interest on the grounds of title by the owner or his/her legal heirs and that term shall begin from the point at which the possession of the defendant becomes adverse to the Plaintiff. So, if the claim for possession is not filed within the prescribed limitation period, then the right of the owner based on the title even if acquired through inheritance shall be extinguished and the person who has possession of the immovable property shall become the owner based on the theory of adverse possession. So, after a lapse of 25 years, the possessor of the property may be considered the owner of the property. So, considering the complexity involved in the matter, it is advisable to hire an experienced property lawyer to navigate the issues in the right way.

question:
A series of crime is committed by accused against me and my brother between 1ST OCTOBER 2019 TO JANUARY 2025. The crimes are of alleged forgery, fraud, cheating, misappropriation, threatening in relation to a property etc. It has come to my knowledge that after 1st July 2024 BNS was introduced. Now in my case crimes were committed by accused during both times that is before 1st July 2024 and after 1st July 2024. That is both Before and After of introduction of BNS ?

Now in January 2025 I want to file my "F.I.R" with police ; so as per which act should I file the complaint BNS or IPC ?

OR to be on the safe should I mention both BNS and IPC sections in my complaint ?
WHAT IS GENERAL PRACTISE IN SUCH CASES . ?( Thane, Maharashtra )
answer: Dear Client,The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) came into force on 1st July, 2024, replacing the Indian Penal Code,1860 and Code of Criminal Procedure,1973 respectively. Questions have arisen regarding whether these new laws apply to offences committed before their effective date of July 1, 2024, and how they impact ongoing proceedings. The Hon'ble Division Bench of Allahabad High Court in the matter of Deepu and Anr. v. State Of U.P . held that while new offences after 01/07/2024 will be governed under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), all offences prior to that date will be governed under the old IPC and Cr. PC. The court observed that if an FIR is registered on or after 1st July, 2024, for an offense committed prior to that date, it should be registered under the provisions of the IPC, but the investigation will proceed as per the BNSS. For investigations pending on 1st July, 2024, the court held that these should continue as per the CrPC until cognizance is taken on the police report. The court clarified that cognizance of pending investigations on or after 1st July, 2024, should be taken as per the BNSS.All subsequent proceedings, including enquiry, trial, or appeal, must be conducted according to the procedure under the BNSS. The court emphasized that despite the repeal of IPC and Cr.PC, liabilities and punishments under the IPC will continue, but procedural aspects will be governed by the BNSS. The Hon'ble  Rajasthan High Court in the case of Krishna Joshi v. State of Rajasthan & Ors. (2024) held that the law applicable on the date of FIR registration will govern the trial, even if it commences after July 1, 2024. The Hon'ble Kerala High Court in the case of Abdul Khader v. State of Kerala (2024)  held that appeals filed on or after July 1, 2024, will be governed by BNSS, regardless of whether the trial was conducted under CrPC. So, given the averments of different High Courts, if you want to file an FIR against a crime in January 2025, that will be registered and tried following the provision of BNS.

question: How many times and in front of whom does the woman victim have to give her statement and appearance after FIR for molestation has been lodged? answer: Dear Client,In this context, Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for Investigation and Prosecution of victims of rape/sexual assault circulated by the Ministry of Home Affairs, Govt of India may be referred wherein it is stated that  1) The victim of such crime should be treated with honor and sensitivity.  The officer interacting with her (the victim) should be extremely courteous. No indecent questions should be put to the victim. Care should be taken to protect dignity and prevent embarrassing situations for the victim. The identity of the victim should not be made public and due care should be taken not to reveal her identity in print and electronic media. 2) A copy of the FIR shall be sent immediately within 24 hours to the Magistrate under Section 157, Cr.P.C. 3) Investigation of crime against women shall be conducted by a woman officer. There should be, at least, one lady officer on the investigating team. 4) As regards the recording of the statement of the victim under section 161, Cr.P.C, the victim should not be called to the police station. The statement of the victim should be recorded at the residence of the victim or in the place of her choice by a woman police officer in the presence of parents or guardians or a near relative or a social worker of the locality. 5) It shall be the duty of the investigating officer/SHO to inform the Judicial Magistrate for the recording of the statement of the person against whom such an offence has been committed, as soon as the commission of offence is brought to the notice of the police (as mandated under sub-section (5-A) of Section 164, Cr.P.C. A copy of the statement under Section 164, Cr.P.C. should be handed over to the investigating officer immediately with specific directions that the content of such statement under Section 164, Cr.P.C. should not be disclosed to any person till the charge sheet/report under Section 173, Cr.P.C. is filed. A copy of the report of the medical examination of the victim, if any, should be immediately handed over to the Magistrate who records Promptly the statement of the victim under section 164, Cr.P.C. In cases of a delay exceeding 24 hours in taking the victim to the Magistrate, the Investigating officer should record the reasons for the same in the case diary and hand over a copy of the same to the Magistrate. 6) Section 164(A),Cr.P.C. imposes an obligation on the part ofinvestigating officer to get the victim of rape medically examined within 24 hours from the time of receiving the information relating to the commission of such offense. The report of such medical examination should be immediately forwarded to the Magistrate by the I.O., who records the statement of the victim under section 164, Cr.P.C. The victim as well as the accused person should be sent for medical examination by the I.O. under a properly filled-in, medicalexamination sheet. The female victim shall be examined medically, only by a lady doctor or under her supervision. A Rape victim above 18 years of age can be examined only after obtaining her written consent. A copy of the report of such examination shall be furnished by the medical officer, or registered medical practitioner, as the case may be, to the victim or her parents/guardian. All offences against women shall be promptly investigated and charge sheets should be filed in the court of law within sixty days as per section 173 Cr.P.C. While briefing media about sex crimes, the identity of the victim should not be disclosed. Under no circumstances, should the victim be produced before the media. Authorized officers alone, should brief the media. Therefore, given the protocol or SPPs of the MHA, if any unethical issues are observed in the investigation by the police, you can file a complaint with the Chairperson, State Human Rights Commission or the State Police Complaint Authority, which are independent bodies empowered to investigate any complaints against police officials. If required, you can hire an Advocate to navigate the issues in the right way.

question: whether we can request the quashing of a different petition within the reply of an existing quashing petition for a different order( New Delhi, Delhi )

The accused can also appraise the Court that there is no material evidence against him even after the investigation into the matter. Another recourse for the accused is to take pleas of inherent improbability on the basis of entire facts and material collected against him in the charge sheet. The Section 482 Cr. PC (replaced by Section 528 of the BNSS) empowers the High Court to dismiss an FIR/criminal proceedings against the accused. It is essential to prove before the court that the FIR was lodged or criminal proceeding was initiated with malicious intent to cause harm or inconvenience and is devoid of truth. The burden of proof rests on the petitioner/appellant. You can file an interlocutory application seeking clubbing of other proceedings or orders passed by the different courts for a summary trial, but the admission of said IA solely depends upon the discretion of the Court and the merit in the application. Appeal and Revision are used to seek a higher court's review of the case and can be filed after the final judgment or order has been passed/issued. The revision can only be sought if the order is considered to be illegal or improper. The power of revision under Section 397 Cr PC is exercised by the High Court in cases where the subordinate court has passed an order in a criminal proceeding. A person is entitled to file only one application for revision in either the court of the session or the High Court. Once a person has applied for revision, he cannot file any other application in any court of law. According to section 397 of Crpc, the High Court and Sessions Judge can exercise the jurisdiction over the revision petition for Corrections, legality, and propriety of an order passed by a trial court. Under Section 397 Cr. PC, the High Court can call for records of a decree passed by any subordinate court if it appears that the lower court has overused jurisdictions, the lower court has misused its jurisdictions and the court has acted unfairly and illegally. According to Article 131 of the Limitation Act 1963, the limitation period for filing a revision petition under Section 397 Cr. P.C. is 90 days from the date of the order under challenge.

The insurance policy may cover third-party liabilities, including compensation to the victim's family.The Motor Vehicles Act requires that third-party insurance covers compensation for victims of road accidents.If negligence is not proven, your father will not have to pay compensation personally; the insurance company will handle it.If negligence is proven, your father may be directed to pay additional compensation, which can be challenged in court.If the case goes to court, it will focus on proving whether your father was negligent.If no substantial evidence of negligence is found, your father may be acquitted.Regards

answer: Dear Client,The essential condition for the application of Section 366 I.P.C. is that there is kidnapping or abduction of a woman with the intention to compel her or knowing it to be likely that she will be compelled to marry any person against her will or will be forced or seduced to illicit intercourse. Section 366 I.P.C. only applies when the woman abducted has no intention of marriage or lawful intercourse when abducted. Mere abduction does not bring the accused under the ambit of this penal section. In Shahjahan Vs. State, 2011 Cr.L.J. 573, the Supreme Court has held that to establish an offence u/s 366 I.P.C., it must first be established that the offence of kidnapping under Section 361 I.P.C. or abduction under Section 362 I.P.C. has been proved. It must then be shown that such kidnapping or abduction was with the contumacious intent referred to under Section 366 I.P.C. Further, in the case of  Gabbu Vs. The state of M.P., AIR 2006 SC 2461, the Apex Court has held that so far as the charge u/s 366 I.P.C. is concerned, mere finding that a woman was abducted is not enough. It must further be proved that the abduction is for the purposes mentioned in Section 366 I.P.C. Given the provision of relevant law and averments of the Apex Court, you can defend your case to before the Court.

question:

I recently filed 317 CRPC and permission to go abroad application in the Magistrate court but it was rejected. 

Please suggest what legal remedies shall I take in this short period of 10 to 12 days of time so I can travel abroad for my work purpose.

answer: Dear Client,A pending criminal case can potentially impact an individual's ability to obtain a visa/passport for abroad. The specific impact will depend on the nature of the crime, the country to which the individual is applying for a passport/visa, and the immigration laws of that country. Every applicant for a passport/visa must go through a thorough process called immigration screening or immigration background checks. Visa/passport authorities often conduct background checks on the documents presented by an applicant to establish strong ties to their home country. you can get a visa/passport issued may be for a short duration even during the pendency of criminal proceedings against you in court or before any law enforcement agency subject to permission of the concerned Court or law enforcement agency where the criminal proceeding is pending. The Allahabad High Court has ruled that a person's application for a visa/passport cannot be withheld merely on the ground that the applicant has a pending criminal case. Further, in the case of Poulami Basu vs The Government of India (2022 SCC OnLine Kar 1606), wherein a single Bench of Karnataka HC held that the right to travel abroad is a fundamental right guaranteed under Article 21 of the Constitution of India. question: I would like to know how many fir i can lodge in a day? May be with same act 173 vnss.( Kolkata, West Bengal )
answer: Dear Client,Section 173 of the BNSS deals with the registration of FIR when information is received regarding the commission of a cognizable offence. The multiple registration of FIR on the same incident or same cause of action is impermissible under the law. No person shall be prosecuted more than once for the same offence. Article 20(2)of the Constitution of India guarantees the right against double jeopardy. When a case has rival versions of each other then two FIRs may be filed for the same and the Police can investigate under both FIRs.

question: CBI acb has initiated a proceedings stating that information was received on 5th but actually it was received on 7th. It was mentioned in the chargesheet that on receiving information on 5th verification was done and subsequently Pre post trap proceedings were initiated. How to get rid of such discrepancy.( Bhubaneswar, Orissa )
answer: Dear Client,The CBI investigates cases of corruption in compliance with the provisions of the Prevention of Corruption Act 1988, under the supervision of the Central Vigilance Commission (CVC). This can include cases of bribery, extortion, and other forms of corruption. The CBI has a special division called the Anti-Corruption Branch (ACB). This branch handles the investigation of corruption-related cases. The CBI can initiate suo moto investigations on the basis of information received from the public, the media, or other sources. CBI lays great emphasis on catching corrupt public servants who demand and take bribes. The process of catching such corrupt public servants red-handed while they demand and take bribes is popularly called the 'trap'. It is not a legal term. A set procedure has been devised in CBI to lay a trap against a corrupt public servant. The evidence collected during the process of trap is placed before the court along with the charge sheet and is quite important in securing the conviction of the public servant charged with corruption. When it was mentioned in the chargesheet that on receiving information on the 5th verification was done and subsequently pre-post trap proceedings were initiated filing chargesheet post verification of the veracity of the information on the 7th, there is prima facie no discrepancy or wrong in the process that requires correction or amendment having no impact at all on the charge brought against the accused. You may, however, raise your voice seeking correction of discrepancy before the authority provided you can prove that with cogent evidence. If required, hire an experience Advocate to navigate the issue.

question: After 4months of matrimonial life, my wife has left my house and went to her parents home. After multiple panchayat of no use, I had given a legal notice to comeback for matrimonial life. But lack of guidance in legal notice I have mentioned her as alcoholic, her short temper behaviour, external affair and her fighting on my parents. Now she had filed a defamation criminal case based on the notice. Unfortunately I don't have enough proofs. Now iam helpless( Hyderabad, Telangana )
answer: Dear Client,Defamation is a civil wrong where the individual rights of a person are infringed. A person can either file a civil suit against the person for defamation or initiate criminal proceedings by filing a complaint as the remedy to defamation under Section 356 of BNS that replaced Section 499 of IPC. Any person who feels their reputation has been damaged by defamatory statements can sue for defamation. The grounds for a defamation case include  1) A defamatory statement that has been made against a person, either written (libel) or spoken (slander),  2) The statement was published or communicated to a third party. 3) The statement caused harm to his/her reputation, 4) There is no valid defense or justification for the defamatory statement. If a person is found guilty of criminal defamation, they can be sentenced to imprisonment for up to two years, a fine, or both. To defend a defamation lawsuit, you need to present evidence in court to prove your innocence and prove that the false accusation made against you never happened or did not happen in the way it is being presented. If required, hire the service of an experienced Advocate to navigate the issue in the right way.

question: What to do if I have been harrased from local money lender, He charged 8% Interest for 15 lakh rupees on every month for 2 years . In asking him to give some time to repay but he's threatening me and my family .( Bangalore, Karnataka )
answer: Dear Client,In India, money lenders are governed by the Money Lenders Act, 1957 in different states. Any individual/organization engaged in a money lending business must hold a license from the appropriate authority such as the RBI or the State Legislature. A money lending license is usually granted by the Revenue Department of the respective state government in compliance with the provision of the Money Lenders Act and the state-specific rules. If any person or a group of persons is involved in trading of money lending or any other financial transaction without any license or permission of the concerned regulatory authority, then he/they may be booked under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002 (PMLA) which was enacted to fight against the criminal offense of legalizing the income/profits from an illegal source, once reported to the vigilance cell. So, in the given scenario, first ensure whether the lender is carrying out his money lending business with a valid license or not, and in the absence of a valid license, serve a legal notice to the lender asking him to refrain from threatening for not payment outstanding of the loan failing which matter may be informed to the concerned regulatory authorities under PMLA and State Revenue Deptt who issues license for money lending business. If required, hire the service of an experienced Advocate to navigate the matter in the right way.

question:
My grandmother had been suffering from heart disease and was recently admitted to the hospital. After a few days, she returned home, still weak and recovering from her illness. On October 29th, our neighbors, who have been causing issues for a long time, started a new dispute about the plastering of our boundary walls. My grandmother overheard the commotion, which was very distressing for her, and she suffered a heart attack and passed away immediately. After her passing, many people came to our house to offer their condolences. During this time, one of our relatives parked his bike in the narrow lane between our houses, which triggered another confrontation with the neighbors. We wanted to file a complaint that day, but we were busy with my grandmother's death rituals. Now, she is trying to frame my cousin as a harasser. What should we do?( Asansol, West Bengal )
answer: Dear Client,To address a false FIR/complaint filed against you, you can seek its quashing through a petition before the High Court under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973(replaced by Section 528 of the BNSS). The Sec.482 Cr. PC (Section 528 of the BNSS) empowers the High Court to dismiss an FIR or criminal proceedings against the accused. It is essential to prove to the court that the FIR was lodged with malicious intent to cause harm or inconvenience and is devoid of truth. The burden of proof rests on the petitioner. An application for the quashing of an FIR or criminal proceedings can also be filed before the High Court under Article 226 of the Constitution of India through a Criminal Miscellaneous Writ Petition invoking the extraordinary jurisdiction of the Court to quash an FIR or criminal proceedings. you can also file a private complaint against your neighbour in the court of the Magistrate under Section 223 of BNSS which outlines the procedure for a Magistrate to take cognizance of an offence. Upon receiving a complaint, the magistrate shall examine the complainant and any witnesses present. This examination is conducted under oath, and the substance of the examination is documented and signed by the complainant, witnesses, and the magistrate. If the magistrate finds sufficient grounds for proceeding with the case, he may issue a summons or warrant to the accused under Section 227 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) 2023. If required, take the service of an experienced lawyer to navigate the issue in the right way.

question: My girlfriend got married with me 2 years ago I have proof now she can't marry me due to her family's disapproval what should I do 8 years of love we still talk( Bankura, West Bengal )
answer: Dear Client,In this context, a recent verdict of the Supreme Court passed in the case of Dolly Rani Vs. Manish Kumar Chanchal Citation: 2024 SCC OnLine SC 754 may be referred to access the status of your case in the given scenario. The Supreme Court said that if a Hindu marriage is not performed following the applicable rites or ceremonies such as 'saptapadi' (taking seven steps by the groom and the bride jointly before the sacred fire), the marriage will not be construed as a Hindu marriage. The Court held that a marriage certificate is valid proof of Hindu marriage only when the marriage ceremony has been performed as per Section 7 of the Court observed that for a valid marriage under the Act, the requisite ceremonies have to be performed and there must be proof of performance of the said ceremony when an issue/controversy arise. Unless the parties have undergone such ceremony, there would be no Hindu marriage according to Section 7 of the Act and a mere issuance of a certificate by an entity in the absence of the requisite ceremonies having been performed, would neither confirm any marital status to the parties nor establish a marriage under Hindu law. In view of the above averment of the Apex Court, even if a marriage certificate is issued on registration of marriage under HMA, in the absence of performance of ceremonies or rites post-registration of marriage cannot be considered a valid marriage. Accordingly,   no legal remedy or relief is feasible in the matter even through litigation.

Please help us we are currently residing in nearby city on rented house and we really want to go back to our hometown.( Hoshangabad, Madhya Pradesh )
answer: Dear Client,In the given scenario, you can file a petition before the Civil Court under Section 37(2) or 38 of the Specific Relief Act, 1963 seeking a permanent injunction on the subject. A permanent injunction, popularly referred to as perpetual injunction, can be granted by the court by passing a decree made after a hearing and upon the merits of the case. Once such decree is passed, the defendant is permanently prohibited from the assertion of a right, or from the commission of an act, which would be contrary to the rights of the plaintiff. The grant of an injunction is subject to the provisions of Order 39, Section 94 (c) and (e) of the Code of Civil Procedure 1908 & Section 37(2) of the Specific Relief Act 1963. Apart from this, you can file a private complaint against the persons who forcefully evicted you from your own house in the court of the Magistrate under Section 223 of BNSS which outlines the procedure for a Magistrate to take cognizance of an offence. Upon receiving a complaint, the magistrate must examine the complainant and any witnesses present. This examination is conducted under oath, and the substance of the examination is documented and signed by the complainant, witnesses, and the magistrate. If the magistrate finds sufficient grounds for proceeding with the case, he may issue a summons or warrant to the accused under Section 227 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) 2023. You can also file a petition praying for an Order of Protection in the City Civil Court or District Court. A Protective Order is a civil court order that is designed to stop violent and harassing behavior and to protect you from the abuser whose attitude or behavior appears to be life-threatening. At the Show Cause hearing, you have to show and prove by adducing substantial evidence why you need the Protective Order. There are no fees for filing a Protective Order. You do not need an Advocate to file for a Protective Order. However, if you wish, you can hire the service of an Advocate to represent you suitably before the Court to obtain a protective order.

question: In the state of Maharastra is there any provision to file online FIR complaint about money laundering instead of registering in person( Raigad, Maharashtra )
answer: Dear Client,An online FIR, also known as an e-FIR, is valid in India. Almost all the state government including the state of Maharashtra has introduced the facility of filing an FIR online to make the process more accessible and efficient for the public. The online FIR is considered as valid as a traditional FIR filed at a police station. In an emergency, the police can register an FIR based on a phone call or e-mail. The FIR should mention the date and time of the incident and the identity of the accused (if known) in a precise manner. After it is registered, the complainant is entitled to a copy free of charge. For serious crimes (cognizable offences), an FIR is required to initiate a police investigation. Visit the Citizen Portal of the Maharashtra Police website (mahapolice.gov.in). Select the âOnline Complaint/e-FIRâ option. Provide accurate information about yourself, the incident, and the parties involved and submit the complaint/FIR. Keep a copy of the acknowledgment or FIR number for reference.

question: I have taken personal loan and 2 credit cards, as my father got severe burnt due to this my financial situation become weak and now unable to pay. Today I got notice from the bank under sector 25 of pssa 2007( Faridabad, Haryana )
answer: Dear Client,Section 25 of the Payment and Settlement System Act 2007(PSSA), states that if an electronic transfer cannot be completed due to insufficient money or if an amount required to be paid out exceeds the limit on the credit card of the payer, the payer can be imprisoned or fined twice the amount or both similar to the dishonor of a cheque under the Negotiable Instruments Act 1881. Section 25 of the Act states that the payee, before filing a complaint under said Act to recover money, must inform the payer via a written notification/legal notice seeking payment of the dishonored amount. If the person initiating an electronic funds transfer does not pay the money to the beneficiary within 15 days of receiving the legal notice, a complaint is filed before the Court for recovery of dues/loan. So, on receipt of notice under Sec.25 of PSSA, you should try your best to negotiate the loan with the lender/financier. You can try to negotiate a debt settlement on your own (under OTS- One-time settlement scheme) if your pocket permits, but sometimes it's typically done through third parties like debt relief companies, which you may hire to negotiate the settlement matter with the lender on your behalf. With this method, you will make payments to the debt settlement company rather than your creditors/lenders, along with the payment of fees or service charges. Debt settlement is an agreement between a lender Bank and a borrower in which the borrower repays a portion of a loan balance and the lender forgives the balance. You may consider starting the negotiation by offering to pay 25% or 30% of your outstanding balance in return for forgiveness on the rest. But, it may be noted that while there are legitimate debt relief/settlement companies, there are also many fraud/scam operations. So, if you're considering one, the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau(CFPB) suggests contacting your state Attorney General's(AG) office and local consumer protection agency to ask if they have any consumer complaints pending on file about that company. Some states require that debt settlement companies be licensed, which may provide some added protection. Although a debt settlement can offload some of your financial burden, there are also a few potential risks and downsides to consider. First, a debt settlement will affect your credit score in CIBIL. That will make it more difficult for you to get credit or good interest rates in the future. Another potential drawback is that when you settle debt, you could face tax consequences. Finally, when you settle a debt with a credit card company, your account is closed once the settlement is complete. So you could potentially have no credit facility to use a credit card further owing to your poor credit score. Further, a quick counseling session with a certified credit counselor can help you discover your options and choose the right path forward.

question: My  cousin was running the chit fund business named affan associate in his name proprietor is his father I was there as a broker there was payment receipt he gives to every investor where at the top affan associates was written and the affan associates named stamp was there but at the received by I have signed in most voucher now he is default and investors are saying I was his partner but there is no partnership deed except that voucher now he is default and out of city with his family and people are torturing me and my father and family what to do now( Kolkata, West Bengal )
answer: Dear Client,Since there is no formal partnership deed or agreement, you cannot be legally held as a partner in the business. Your cousin's father, as the sole proprietor of the chit fund business, is legally responsible for the company's liabilities.Your role as a broker was to facilitate transactions, but that does not make you liable for the business debts. However, your signatures on the receipts could complicate matters as it gives the appearance of involvement in the transactions. Nonetheless, without a legal partnership agreement, mere signatures on receipts do not establish liability in a chit fund default.Steps to Protect Yourself Legally:File a Police Complaint: Since you and your family are being harassed and tortured by investors, you should file a police complaint against those harassing you. Include details of the threats and any unlawful behavior from the investors. This will provide immediate protection for you and your family.Legal Notice: Send a legal notice to the investors (through a lawyer) explaining that you are not a partner and that the chit fund business was solely owned by your cousinâs father. Highlight the fact that no legal partnership deed exists and that your involvement was limited to facilitating transactions.Clarify Your Role in Writing: If your cousin is unreachable, you can issue a public statement through your lawyer or inform the police about your limited role as a broker and not as a partner. This will help create a legal trail showing you were not directly responsible for the financial decisions or defaults of the business.Contract Law Defense: If investors attempt to file a civil suit against you, you can defend yourself by arguing that:You were not a formal partner or co-owner.There was no contract or agreement that held you responsible for business debts.Your signatures were merely administrative and did not indicate partnership.Indian Partnership Act, 1932: Under this law, without a partnership deed, you are not liable for the firmâs debts or liabilities. You can cite this law to defend yourself.Legal Action Against the Chit Fund Proprietor (Your Cousin's Father)If needed, you can also file a police complaint or a civil suit against your cousin and his father (the proprietor of the chit fund) for fraud or misrepresentation if they left you in a vulnerable position or used your name to defraud investors.Release of Liability: Once itâs clear that you were not a partner, you should not be held liable for the debts. Investors may need to pursue your cousin and his father legally to recover their money.Criminal Charges Against Your Cousin: If your cousinâs family has absconded, they could face criminal charges for fraud and mismanagement of funds. This will relieve you from further pressure.Civil Case Against You (If Any): In case the investors file a civil suit against you, they would need to prove that you were a partner. Without a partnership deed or any written proof, they are unlikely to succeed.Regards

question: Can pre-litigation mediation be an option when I'm certain no offense(compoundable) has occurred, but to settle the matter completely before any takes legal action? If yes, who can be the mediator and what is the process?( Guwahati, Assam )
answer: Dear Client,Lok Adalats can deal with civil matters as well as criminal matters which are compoundable under any law. They have no jurisdiction in respect of matters relating to divorce or matters relating to an offence not compoundable under any law. On receipt of an application from any one of the parties to any matter referred to in clause (ii) of sub-section (5) of section 19 of the Legal Services Authorities Act 1987 that such matter needs to be determined by a Lok Adalat, refer such matter to the Lok Adalat, for determination. Accordingly, a Notice under Sub-Sec. 2 of Section 20 of the Act is issued to both parties advising them to appear before the Lok Adalat organized by the Legal Services Authority under sub-section (1) of Section 19 of the Act. In Lok Adalat, the emphasis is placed on persuading the parties to arrive at a settlement. Every Lok Adalat shall have the requisite powers to specify its own procedure for the determination of any dispute coming before it and Lok Adalat shall have the same powers as are vested in a Court under the CPC, 1908 and Cr.PC 1973. Every award made by a Lok Adalat shall be final and binding on all the parties to the dispute, and no appeal shall lie to any court against the award passed by a Lok Adalat which is constituted for the speedy disposal of pending cases and is an alternate dispute redressal system of a judicial body or quasi-judicial body. Lok Adalat is one of the alternative dispute redressal mechanisms, it is a forum where disputes/cases pending in the court of law or at the pre-litigation stage are settled/ compromised amicably. As per Section 20(3) in The Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987, where any case is referred to a Lok Adalat under sub-section (1) or where a reference has been made to it under sub-section (2), the Lok Adalat shall proceed to dispose of the case or matter and arrive at a compromise or settlement between the parties. If require, you mah hire the service of an Advocate to navigate the matter in the right way.

answer: Dear Client,The High Court under Section 482 of the Cr. PC has the power to quash an FIR even after filing of Charge Sheet by the prosecution. Another recourse for the accused is to take pleas of inherent improbability on the basis of entire facts and material collected against him in the charge sheet. The Section 482 Cr. PC (replaced by Section 528 of the BNSS) empowers the High Court to dismiss an FIR/criminal proceedings against the accused. It is essential to prove before the court that the FIR was lodged or criminal proceeding was initiated with malicious intent to cause harm or inconvenience and is devoid of truth. The burden of proof rests on the petitioner/appellant. question: The family in my neighborhood had been pressuring me to vacate the house for several months. Gradually, it escalated to misbehavior, abuse, and death threats. So, my mother filed an FIR against them. A month later, they filed a counter FIR against me and lodged a case under the SC/ST Act. Charges like 147, 323, 504, 506, 3(1)da, 3(1)dha etc., have been registered. The police did not arrest me, but the case is now in court, and the first hearing is in October. What should I do?( Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh )
answer: Dear Client,In the given scenario, you should first apply for anticipatory bail before the Court of Session or High Court. Before an arrest is made, anticipatory bail can be obtained under Section 438 of the Cr. PC by approaching the Court of Session or the High Court. The powers of the High Court in granting bail are very wide; even so where the offenses are non-bailable. To address a false FIR or false criminal proceedings filed against you, you can seek its quashing through a petition before the High Court under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973(now Sec.528 of BNSS). The Section 482 Cr. PC empowers the High Court to dismiss false FIR/criminal proceedings initiated under that FIR/complaint before the trial Court against a person. It is essential to prove before the court that the FIR/complaint or criminal suit was lodged with malicious intent to cause harm or inconvenience and is devoid of truth. The burden of proof rests on the petitioner. You can file a private complaint against your errant and unruly neighbour in the court of the Magistrate under Section 223 of BNSS which outlines the procedure for a Magistrate to take cognizance of an offence. Upon receiving a complaint, the magistrate shall examine the complainant and any witnesses present. This examination is conducted under oath, and the substance of the examination is documented and signed by the complainant, witnesses, and the magistrate. If the magistrate finds sufficient grounds for proceeding with the case, they will issue a summons or warrant to the accused under Section 227 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) 2023. If required take the service of an experienced criminal lawyer to navigate the issue in the right way.

question: Can a primary petition be moved before hearing final appeal, highlighting grave errors in trial court judgment?( Kochi, Kerala )
answer: Dear Client,Yes, a primary petition can be filed before the appellate court to assert foul play in a trial court judgment even when a final appeal is pending. Rule 27 of the Order 41 of the CPC, 1908 permits the tendering of additional evidence or additional grounds for such reasons as may be necessary having reference to questions of law and fact involving substantial importance to the case which were not raised or, urged at the hearing of the former appeal. Where the errors are serious on the trail court the affected party could approach the appellate court through a Special Leave Petition SLP under Article 136 of the Constitution of India to draw the attention of the appellate court to them. question: My wife filed 498 against me and my sister.now she want to close the case. answer: Dear Client,A lawyer cannot act in a dual capacity being that of a constituted attorney of the party as well as an advocate in the same matter. Any advocate who is engaged by a client would have to play only one role, i.e., that of the advocate in the proceedings and cannot act as a power of attorney holder and verify pleadings and file applications or any other documents or give evidence on behalf of his client which is contrary to the provisions of the Advocates Act, 1961. Like a General Power of attorney, a Special power of attorney is one by which a person is appointed by the principal to do some specified act or acts. In this type of power of attorney, an agent is conferred with the power to do a specific act in a single or specified transaction in the name of the principal. Recently in a case, the Supreme Court observed that Section 32 Of the Advocates Act, 1961 does not create a bar for a General Power of Attorney or Special Power of Attorney holder to appear on behalf of a plaintiff. Accordingly, your sister can execute a GPA or SPA  appointing you as constituted attorney to appear before the court on the scheduled date of hearing and take steps on her behalf. The GPA/SPA should be registered under the Registration Act to make it legally valid and enforceable under the law.

question:
Case Summary: A doctor performed a cesarean section on a patient early in the morning on the 5th. On the afternoon of the 6th, the doctor had to leave for another state but remained reachable by phone. The patientâs condition was stable, with normal reports until the morning of the 7th, when she suddenly died due to vasovagal obstruction or sudden cardiac arrest. During the doctorâs absence, the patient was monitored by qualified GNM nursing staff, and when complications arose, the doctor advised them to administer oxygen over the phone. As the situation worsened, other unaffiliated doctors were called, who administered emergency interventions, including adrenaline, but the patient unfortunately passed away.

Following this, a medical negligence case was filed against the doctor. The medical board, after reviewing the treatment, did not find any evidence of improper care. However, the lower court found the doctor negligent, primarily due to the fact that she did not appoint another doctor to oversee the patientâs care in her absence, despite being instantly reachable by phone and the patient being under the care of qualified nursing staff.

Key Issues for Consideration:

 Is the courtâs focus on the absence of a physically present doctor justified, even when the doctor was reachable and nursing staff were qualified to handle routine care? How do you interpret the balance between a doctorâs remote availability and the necessity of a physical handover in ensuring the continuity of care?( Nagaur, Rajasthan )
answer: Dear Client,A doctor's physical and remote availability, especially in an emergency, differs and potentially affects the treatment of a critical post-surgery case. The physical presence of a qualified doctor cannot be compared with unqualified doctors or even qualified nursing staff considering the distinct nature of skill and efficiency required to treat and resolve a patient's critical condition. Medical negligence is proved beyond doubt when a qualified doctor fails to engage a qualified doctor to treat a patient in critical condition and continues with his or her remote service engaging unqualified doctors to treat the patient who succumbed for lack of proper treatment. The essential ingredients of Section 304A of IPC are that (1) There must be the death of a person; (2) The death must be caused by the act of the accused; (3) The death must be caused due to any rash or negligent act of the accused; and (4) the act of the accused must not amount to culpable homicide. Section 304A of the IPC may attract even in cases where the doctor delegated his responsibility to another person. The Supreme Court in the case of M/s. Spring Meadows Hospital & Anr v. Harjol Ahluwalia through K.S. Ahluwalia & Anr. (1998) held that where the senior pediatrician delegated his duty to a junior and the senior doctor is aware that the junior has no capacity and sufficient skill to perform such duty properly, the senior doctor is said to be negligent by delegating his work to an incompetent person. So, the observation and order of the trial Court holding the treating doctor accused of medical negligence under Section 304A of IPC stands reasonable and justified.

I went to file revision u/s 397 crpc but the reader told me this is an interlocutory order and revision can not be filed

now i have mentioned the below line in my revision petition, will it remove the bar of interlocutory order?
This order affects the rights of the women to get her own jewelry property/Stridhan due to this above-mentioned order would not be an interlocutory order and the present revision is not barred u/s 397(2).

the lower court order is intermediate or interlocutory order?( Gurgaon, Haryana )
answer: Dear Client,An order of dismissal of a case is a procedural termination without a decision on the merits and is considered an interlocutory order and a revision petition under Sec.397(2) of Cr. PC is not maintainable. An order that does not determine the rights of the parties but only one aspect of the suit or the trial is an interlocutory order. However, in the case of Amarnath and Ors. Vs. State of  Haryana and Anr., (1977) 4 SCC 137 the Hon'ble Supreme Court has defined interlocutory order stating that interlocutory orders must be those which decide the rights and liabilities of the parties which are purely interim or temporary in nature and do not decide or touch the important rights or liabilities of the parties. .Any order that substantially affects the rights of the accused, or decides certain rights of the parties cannot be said to be an interlocutory order so as to bar a revision to the High Court against that order, because that would be against the very object which formed the basis for insertion of this particular provision in Section 397 of the 1973 Code. Thus, orders which are matters of moment and which affect or adjudicate the rights of the accused on a particular aspect of the trial cannot be said to be interlocutory so as to be outside the purview of the revisional jurisdiction of the High Court.

question:
If fIR is registered under sec 420,467,468,471,120b and the I.O of the case sends sec 161 notice to the accused and they received it but didnt appread on the prescribed date ..then again IO send them 161 notice but they didnt came and also didnt received the notice and then IO send them last notice which is on 12 august 2024..
what if they didnt appread on that day too?( Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh )
answer: Dear Client,Section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 allows an investigating officer to question a person who is supposed to be familiar with the facts and circumstances of the case. The purpose of section 161 is to acquire evidence that can later be used in court. Recording of statements under Sections 161 by  IO and 164 of Cr.P.C. by the Magistrate, plays a pivotal role in criminal trial. The purpose of contradiction between the evidence of a witness before the court and the statement recorded under Section 161 and 164 of Cr.P.C is primarily to shake the credit of the witness, it is only to put the court on guard, to scrutinize the evidence with great care. If the witnesses did not turn up on receipt of notice issued under Section 161 Cr.PC on repeated occasions, the IO may request the Magistrate for issue of summons to the concerned persons for recording their statement. A summon is a court order for an individual to appear in court at a specified time and place. Every summon shall be served by a police officer, or by an officer of the court issuing it or any other public servant. A summon may be issued in both criminal and civil cases. Order V Rule 9 of the CPC provides exhaustive stipulations for the service of summons to the respondent to be carried out by the court. Where such summons have been served by the court under Order V, but are returned undeliver on account of the change of address or addressee/respondent left the place, the court may pass an order for publication in the popular newspaper. In case the service of summons is evaded by the respondent, the court may issue bailable or non-bailable warrants against the respondent. If any court has reason to believe that any person against whom a warrant has been issued has absconded or is concealing himself so that such warrant cannot be executed, such court may publish a written proclamation requiring him to appear at a specified place and time within 30 days of publishing such proclamation. The Court issuing a proclamation may, at any time after the issue of the proclamation, order the attachment of any property, movable or immovable or both, belonging to the proclaimed person.

If your brother has withdrawn money post your fatherâs death using the debit card, it could be considered a criminal act of fraud or cheating ( Section 318 , BNS) , misappropriation of funds (section 314, BNS) and criminal breach of trust (section 316, BNS). Cost of the criminal process may vary depending upon the complexity of the case. Capital punishment is not given in such financial fraud cases. Waiting for succession certificate may give your brother more time to manipulate the situation and create nuisance. As a class I legal heir, you have the right to access the account information and gather statement. Obtain a court order to compel the bank for giving you the statement. answer: Dear Client,In the hit-and-run case, police filed an FIR on both the persons involved in a road accident under Sec. 279 of IPC(now Section 281 of BNS) for rash and negligent driving and Section 337 of IPC (now Section 125 of BNS)  for causing hurt to any person. Both offenses are cognizable and bailable offence and triable by a Magistrate. On appeal, bail can be provided by the police officer who has custody of the offender or by the court. To obtain bail, a bail bond needs to be executed, with or without the presence of sureties.   In motor accident cases both the owner and driver of the vehicle are liable to face prosecution proceedings initiated before the Motor Accident Claim Tribunal once an FIR is lodged in the police station in hit and run case and the legal heirs of the deceased victim and the injured persons apply to the Tribunal under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 within six months of the occurrence of the accident.  Section 164 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (as amended in 2019) states that the owner of the motor vehicle or the authorized insurer shall be liable to pay compensation of five lakh rupees in case of death or two and a half lakh rupees in case of grievous hurt to the legal heirs or the victim, as the case may be. The claimant is not required to prove that the death or grievous hurt was due to any wrongful act or neglect of the owner or any other person. In this context, the judgment passed by the Calcutta High Court in the case of Senjuti Roy (Nee Sengupta) VS New India Assurance Co. Ltd. and the judgment passed by the Rajasthan High Court in the case of Ganesh Bairwa VS Ramphool Bairwa may be referred. Given the complexity of the motor accident case as stated in the query that involves delayed registration of the vehicle, driving a vehicle on the road without insurance and other vital documents, absconding of a vehicle in hit and run case, contradictory statements of the witnesses and finally the investigation report of the police, the Tribunal may pass an order for payment of compensation to the claimant against the defaulted parties. Fine as a penalty is imposed only if there is a criminal prosecution. You have to establish the fact before the Court denying that you were not driving the vehicle rashly and that the accident arose not on account of your negligence. You have to take the defense that in spite of cautious driving you met with an accident. Unless you plead guilty generally fine is not imposed. The maximum fine for both offences is around Rs.1500. under Section 279 and 337 IPC if you are ready to plead guilty then the court will impose the fine and close the case but it is better if you can engage the service of an Advocate to navigate the issue in the right way. You may like to contest the case but the court case will drag you for years and you may have to waste your time, energy, and money on litigation as well as lawyer fees which may be ten times the amount that you may pay as a fine, hence better pay the fine amount, which appears to be very minimum and come out of this crisis.

answer: Dear Client,Indian penal Code (IPC) is now Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). Section 316, BNS lays down Criminal breach of trust. Your wife has cheated over you and occurred you wrongful loss. Under these sections, you may file criminal case against her act. Regarding the time gap from 2022 to 2024, considering the statute of limitations, the period of limitation prescribed for taking cognizance in respect of an offence of the criminal breach of trust for which the maximum punishment is imprisonment for three years is ordinarily three years. Therefore, if the case is filed within three years, you are within the limitation period. Along with criminal case, you may also file civil case for recovering your property. question: What happens with a group of people to whom BNS Act. U/S. 126 (2), 115 (2), 117 (2) & 3 (5) is imposed? Can police arrest them? Can police show softness to them by letting them free and take bail? Bail can be granted by how many days?( Jalpaiguri, West Bengal )
answer: Dear Client,Section 126(2) of BNS deals with wrongful restraint and punishment for wrongful restraint. Section  115 (2) of BNS deals with Voluntarily causing hurt and punishment for the said offence and Section 117 (2) of BNS deals with  Voluntarily causing grievous hurt and punishment for the same. Section 3(5) of BNS deals with acts done by several persons in furtherance of common intention. Under Section 126(2) of BNS, the offense is Cognizable and bailable and punishable by simple imprisonment for up to one month, a fine of up to five thousand rupees, or both. Section 115(2) is a non-cognizable and bailable offense. Section 117(2) is a Cognizable. and bailable offense punishable with imprisonment for 7 years and a fine.  Section 3(5) of BNS is a cognizable and bailable offense. A police officer knowing of a design to commit any cognizable offense may arrest, without orders from a Magistrate and a warrant, if it appears to such officer that the commission of the offense cannot be otherwise prevented. Before an arrest is made, anticipatory bail is granted under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. For bailable offenses, the accused can be released on bail without going through a court trial. In non-bailable offenses, the accused must attend court proceedings and apply for bail in front of a judge. In bailable offenses, the court has the discretion to grant or deny bail based on the circumstances. If required hire the service of an Advocate to navigate the offense in the right way.

question: i have question whether "against order of sec 145crpc by the executive magistrate the revision is maintanable or Appeal is maintanable? please elaborate the reasons also( Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh )
answer: Dear Client,Both Appeal and Revision are legal remedies that allow a person to challenge a decision or judgment made by a lower court or tribunal. Both Appeal and Revision are used to seek a higher court's review of the case and can be filed after the final judgment or order has been passed/issued. The revision can only be sought if the order is considered to be illegal or improper. The power of revision under Section 397 is exercised by the High Court in cases where the subordinate court has passed an order in a criminal proceeding. A person is entitled to file only one application for revision in either the court of the session or the High Court. Once a person has applied for revision, he cannot file any other application in any court of law. According to section 397 of Crpc, the High Court and Sessions Judge can exercise the jurisdiction over the revision petition for Corrections, legality, and propriety of an order passed by a trial court. Under Section 379 Cr. PC, the High Court can call for records of a decree passed by any subordinate court if it appears that the lower court has overused jurisdictions, the lower court has misused its jurisdictions and the court has acted unfairly and illegally. According to Article 131 of the Limitation Act 1963, the limitation period for filing a revision petition under Section 397 Cr. P.C. is 90 days from the date of the order under challenge.
